standard.title: Create texts using varied structures and conventions
standard.description: create and present a range of informative and imaginative spoken, written and multimodal texts using a variety of modelled sentence structures to sequence information and ideas, and conventions appropriate to text type
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create informative and imaginative texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and modelled conventions (AC9LS4C05). They create for familiar formats. They have not yet used varied structures to sequence ideas, applied procedural text conventions, or created diary entries using past tense.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and present a range of informative and imaginative texts using varied modelled sentence structures to sequence information and ideas, with conventions appropriate to text type.

nodes.label: Sequencing ideas using varied sentence structures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create texts that sequence information and ideas using varied sentence structures — including time markers, connectors and tense variation — not only isolated statements.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text using at least three different sentence structures with ideas presented in a logical sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Use varied structures to sequence information — time markers, connectors, sequencing adverbs; use tense variation for temporal meaning; apply procedural text conventions (imperative forms, step language, quantities); create diary or journal entries; use thought bubbles and commentary in visual text formats.
wider: Create a text using at least three different tenses coherently — explaining the temporal purpose of each tense choice
Create a procedural text for a real activity applying all the features of the text type — imperative forms, sequence adverbs, quantities
nodes.hinge_reason: Sequencing ideas across sentence boundaries is the structural move from sentence-level to text-level production. Students who produce only isolated sentences cannot create coherent texts — which is required for all text creation from this band onwards.

response_modes.reason: Text-level coherence requires explicit awareness of the sequencing devices that connect sentences into a whole. Students need to see and practise each device deliberately before coherent multi-sentence production becomes automatic.

success_criteria: Creates a text with at least three sentences logically connected using time markers, connectors or tense variation
Uses at least two different sentence structures across the text

nodes.label: Applying text-type conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create texts in a range of formats — applying conventions appropriate to each text type for purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Create texts in at least two different formats using at least one text-type-specific convention in each.
nodes.typical_width: Create digital profiles, event materials, diary entries, instructive texts, comic strips, cultural presentations, performance scripts; apply conventions specific to each text type — diary informality, advertisement persuasion, instruction imperatives; create bilingual materials for younger learners.
wider: Create a text for a genuine audience outside the classroom — adapt text-type conventions specifically for that audience and reflect on what was changed
Compare two texts created for different purposes on the same topic — explain every difference in convention, register and structure

response_modes.reason: Text-type convention competence develops through creating across varied formats and purposes. Students who only create one text type develop narrow production schemas.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Applying different conventions for different text types is where students begin to understand that language choices are purposeful — that the same content sounds different in a diary, an advertisement and a procedure.
success_criteria: Creates texts in at least two different formats with appropriate conventions for each
At least one text-type convention is consistently applied throughout each text

nodes.label: Presenting for real audiences and purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present texts to real audiences — using deliberate delivery choices for voice, visual support and performance — and create texts that serve genuine communicative purposes.
nodes.minimum_width: Present at least one text to a genuine audience using at least one deliberate delivery choice.
nodes.typical_width: Present informative and imaginative texts to varied real audiences; create and perform original texts for community events, school activities or younger learners; create First Nations Country/Place descriptions for real contexts; produce target language content for genuine publication or display.
wider: Create and perform an original text in the target language for a real purpose — demonstrating deliberate selection of text type, register and conventions for the audience
Create a text presented to an audience outside the school community — reflecting on how the audience affected language choices

response_modes.reason: Presenting for real audiences integrates all prior text creation work — sequencing (N1) and text-type conventions (N2) — and deploys them for genuine communicative purpose. The real audience is the integration test.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creating for real audiences — performances, community events, genuine publications — is where target language use becomes genuinely purposeful. Students at this level are ready to produce content that matters beyond the classroom.
success_criteria: Presents a text to a genuine audience using at least one deliberate delivery choice
The text serves its intended communicative purpose for the audience
